findings.G1_SEWING: Owner D14-14 gap G1: the connected WIP & Sewing screen records SELESAI DIJAHIT for a picked-up Potongan (as the UX demo card does) through one Native step: a POSTED work completion (piece-work wage to the Mandor payable) and the sewing terminal event that Laundry counts as ready to send; cancel only while the pieces are still at the Mandor and the wage is outside payroll and any active attendance pool; base-component rates only (SKU-wave rates refused as WAVE_SKU_RATES), a PO model without a Work BOM refused as NO_WORK_RATE; before the first record the screen shows the estimated wage from the rates the Native snapshot would take (Mandor rate, else Work BOM default), and the outcome reports the wage actually posted

findings.R2_01_CASH: Round dfab13bf, owner D15-1: Fable FABLE-013 (the D14-3 guard judged only the economic date while the owner cash report uses the book date; a closed-period income booked today let an expense leave yesterday at -500) and Sol SOL-R1-001 (a correction of an income already spent was refused on its half-way balance, before its replacement). The guard now judges both dates, and the customer payment correction, misc correction and sales note correction open a compound scope so the guard judges their end state; a scope left open refuses the whole transaction at commit; the detector lists both dates. Fable's and Sol's scenarios run with their own amounts.
findings.R2_06_SERIES: Round dfab13bf: Astra ASTRA-C17-01 (a series was keyed by the commercial SKU text alone, so the same SKU number of a second brand joined the first brand's series) and ASTRA-C17-02 (the invoice could be saved while the other sizes of a picked series were still loading). The connected sales screen keys a series by brand name plus commercial SKU from the server row, cancels the review the moment a pick starts and blocks saving until the sizes are in. The D14-5 browser fixture adds a second brand with the same series SKU (size 32, stock 5) that must stay out of the invoice with its stock unchanged.
findings.R2_05_PO: Round dfab13bf: Astra ASTRA-C17-05 (the PO finish panel called the HPP final while the server said BELUM_LENGKAP/ESTIMATED, and its workspace said eligible while Native refused: six cut pieces neither sewn-and-sent nor through direct QC) and Fable FABLE-014 (no way to reopen a finished PO from the app; the source comment wrongly said no Native inverse exists). The finish workspace now carries the exact predicate of Native erp.guard_finished_po_source_accounting (SOURCE_UNACCOUNTED), the panel words the HPP from display_status only, and po-reopen.sql reopens through Native erp.reopen_production_order with a review token, reason, idempotency, immutable history and three blockers (NOT_FINISHED, FG_USED, PERIOD_CLOSED). Astra's three journeys run with her own arithmetic; Fable's D15-4 oracle (reopen, ledger-consistent WIP, same HPP on finishing again, two tabs one winner, HTTP, browser) is covered.
findings.R2_03_MASTER: Round r2: Fable FABLE-017, Astra ASTRA-C17-04 and the known daily-master gap: customers, suppliers/laundry vendors, Mandor (dated attendance/Special policy), warehouses/locations, fabric (profile, benchmark price versions) and accessories (category, variant, Mandor price) had no connected screen, and a new Mandor or model had no rate for "Catat selesai jahit". master.sql and rates.sql add one closed facade per screen over the Native writers and guards (review token, reason, idempotency, immutable history, used records cannot change code/type/unit or be deactivated while open or stocked, nothing is ever deleted), Mandor work rates per model x work component from a date, and the model's Work BOM. The sewing workspace now previews the rates valid at the sewing time entered (rate_timeline, Native snapshot rule) instead of today's. Fable's D15-3 oracle: every master screen on desktop and phone, HTTP, two tabs per screen, and the screen-only chain new Mandor + new rate -> Bagi Potongan -> Catat selesai jahit paying the rate valid on the sewing date, a later rate change leaving the recorded wage unchanged. CI run 38861916560 (109/113): a stocked warehouse from older data whose code is stored in lower case could not be edited at all, because the facade upper-cases codes and then read the stored code in another case as a code change of a used record; the stored code in another case is now no code change and is kept exactly as stored (Native case and the stocked-warehouse browser step).
findings.R2_04_AUTO_PO: Round r2: Sol SOL-R1-002, owner D15-6. Buat Potongan had no way to make the PO the cutting belongs to; a new model needed a PO made elsewhere first. auto-po.sql (schema cp7_cutting_correction) adds one closed facade: a draft lives only in the facade (no PO, stock or journal); POST takes the next free PO number of the cutting day (WIB) under an advisory lock, inserts the PO as the Native lifecycle requires (DRAFT at CUTTING), posts the cutting through the Native writer erp_save_cutting_group_before_sewing_v2 in the same transaction and returns the PO number; any Native refusal (roll not available, cutting time in the future, size outside the model) leaves no PO, no stock movement and the number unused; the same UUID returns the stored answer and a changed payload under it is refused. Tests: one transaction, same UUID same answer (Native, two tabs, real-Auth HTTP, and on screen after a lost answer), failure midway, draft without effect, access rights, then Bagi Potongan and Catat selesai jahit on the new PO.
findings.R2_11_CUTOVER: Fable FABLE-011, owner D15-5: there was no global cutover floor for writers that bring in goods or value. cutover.sql (schema cp7_cutover): the owner sets the official date (WIB) in the app on the Impor data awal page, with an immutable history, idempotent per actor and request; the date may not lie after the first operational day already in the books nor after any import batch cutover. Until set nothing changes. Once set, BEFORE INSERT triggers refuse journal entries (economic date) and material/FG stock movements (WIB date of physical_at) dated before it, whichever writer inserts them, except the opening/migration postings and inverses of existing rows; an import batch may not take an earlier cutover date. Postings and the owner change serialise on one control row. Tests: the date boundary (00:00 on the day posts, 23:59:59 the day before is refused, for a journal and for stock), the opening path (import at the official date, original receipt date kept, late invoice after cutover, settlement after cutover, GRNI/AP once, reversal on its path), failure in the middle of a correction (nothing stays), resending (same answer; a refused request stays refused), two tabs, setting against a posting of the day before, real-Auth HTTP, and the screen on desktop and phone.
findings.R2_10_WAVE: Sol KNOWN-BF-WAVE (S1): a Potongan bound to SKU waves (BF commercial ranges) could not record SELESAI DIJAHIT (WAVE_SKU_RATES). Now RECORD_WAVE records pieces per SKU of the wave (each SKU covering its bound sizes) in one transaction: per SKU one work completion on that SKU's Native snapshot (erp.bf_ensure_work_v1 through the same ensure; SKU rate per component, else the base rate) and its SELESAI_DIJAHIT; per-SKU remaining = pieces cut in its sizes minus what is already completed/payable per component (the Native per-SKU guard). Before the first record the screen shows per SKU the rates the Native snapshot takes at the sewing time entered (sewing_wave_at, compared with the Native writer at four instants). The single-quantity base path refuses a wave Potongan (CP7_SEWING_WAVE_PER_SKU); a Native base-rate line on it stays refused (BF_WORK_SCOPE_REQUIRED).
findings.R2_07_SCREEN_CHAIN: FABLE-016 (S3), ASTRA-C17-07 (S2), Sol BROWSER-CHAIN: one browser chain on the screens only, from masters and opening WIP created on 'Impor data awal' (CSV files, check, post) to 'Rincian produksi awal' (WIP to brand-A goods), 'Ganti Merek' (to brand B), 'Laporan & Tutup Buku' (books closed through that day in the middle of the chain), 'Penjualan & Invoice' and its payment into a bank, and the books reopened; the closed days' books stay exactly as closed. Fixture only for a bank account (no screen) and harness state (chain month opened, seed open items cleared, restored). Second chain, same start: the imported Mandor's work component and rate on 'Master Data → Mandor', 3 WIP pieces split off as BS ('Pisahkan sebagai BS'), the imported product's accessory recipe declared without accessories on 'Produk & SKU' (a rework needs the product's accessory BOM valid when it is sent; the SKU master writes it from now on, so the rework is sent now), the BS case classified with that component (none done before the BS; a piece split off from opening WIP carries no work component), a rework order to that Mandor with the component as wage basis and its result on 'Barang BS & Rework', the rework wage in a Nota posted to payroll ('Susun Nota FG'), the payroll counted, approved and paid ('Payroll & Kasbon'); fixture adds owner capital for exactly that wage. Attendance HPP pool: no screen runs that cycle and r2 adds none; it stays a recorded open boundary, not an owner decision. Context only, owner D15-2 on the attendance screens in Enteng, verbatim: "sembunyikan begitu terhubung langsung muncul, doesnt matter juga kalau mau langsung muncul karena gabakal dipakai juga jadi ga kerja 2 kali sih klo mau munculin".
findings.R3_01_AUTO_PO_NUMBER: Astra ASTRA-R2-02 (S1), Sol SOL-R2-001 (S2), candidate 2e9d6a46: the automatic PO number of Buat Potongan could not pass 999 on one cutting day, because auto-po.sql formatted it with lpad(n,3), which cuts 1000 to 100, so the search for a free number never ended (statement timeout; nothing was left behind). Three digits is now the minimum width. The auditors' own failing cases are used as written: Sol's 998 and 999 unused DRAFT headers with a 3 s limit (999 and 1000 must be made), Astra's empty day with 998 headers then 999 and 1000 (roll 10 -> 8 -> 6) under a 10 s limit; plus 1001 and 9999 -> 10000, a refused post that uses no number and a resend with the same UUID past 1000, and two sessions posting at the 999/1000 boundary (two distinct numbers, both posted).
findings.R3_02_PO_REOPEN_ACTIVE_USE: Astra ASTRA-R2-01 (S1), candidate 2e9d6a46: the FG_USED blocker of the PO reopen (owner D15-4) summed every historical outflow of the PO's production lots, so a cancelled sales draft or a reversed finished-goods adjustment kept the PO blocked forever. It now counts only use that is still active: an outflow minus what its own reversals (reversal_of_id) put back; an unrelated inflow never offsets an active use. Astra's two cases are used as written (cancelled draft: stock 10 -> 8 -> 10, accounts as before; reversed -2 adjustment: stock and HPP as before, account delta of Native sync_po_hpp_to_gl that Astra qualified), plus controls: an active draft still blocks, a +2 adjustment does not offset an active 2-piece draft, cancelling one of two drafts leaves the other blocking (5 then 3), reopen after the cancel then finish again gives the same stock and HPP, and two tabs reopen once.
findings.R3_09_RATE_CHOICE: Owner D16-2, D16-3, D16-4 (not an audit finding): when the Mandor rate in force at a later sewing time differs from the rate the PO locked at its first wage, the record pays the locked rate or the new one by explicit choice (refused without one, and refused with one where the rates are equal or the PO is switched); 'Pakai tarif baru seterusnya' switches the PO once, with a reason, never undone, after which records take the new rate without asking. Only Owner/Admin record or switch. A new rate is paid through a rate revision row of the PO snapshot written only by the CP7 command (declared Native deltas cp7_rate_revision_bundle.py: snapshot index gains committed_at, bf_ensure_work_v1 pins new SKUs from original base rows, prepare_rework_component_line SKU branch and seed_bs_case_component_baseline take the latest row; the index restore refuses while revisions exist). Cases: same rate no choice, changed rate needs a choice, OLD and NEW wages from Native lines and journals, revision reuse per sewing time, switch and its refusals, D16-4 role refusal, cancel of a new-rate record, payroll pipeline and unchanged Native detectors, wave per SKU, declared deltas and restore refusal, immutable private tables; two tabs choosing NEW, switch against record; real Auth HTTP; browser desktop and phone.
findings.R3_03_PERIOD_TAB: Owner D16-5 (not an audit finding): "Tutup Periode" is no longer a menu; closing the books is the "Tutup Buku" tab of "Laporan & Tutup Buku", the old route opens that tab. The period workspace adds the close/reopen history from the Native audit rows the accepted writers record for erp.accounting_period_control (column grants only); the oracle reads erp.audit_logs and erp.app_users directly and derives CLOSE/REOPEN itself. Rights stay separate: the report needs finance.reports.view, the tab and the facade also need finance.period_close.manage; seeded ADMIN (report right, no close right) is refused the period workspace natively and over real Auth, reads the report without the close check, and sees no tab in the browser.
findings.R3_03_ENTENG_BUILD: Owner D16-1 (Fable oracle 2, 3, 5): every CP17 browser case runs a second time on the Enteng build (UAT_AUTH_SIMULATION, the same build as the Enteng deployment except a placeholder publishable key), against a fresh disposable copy; the browser answers the Enteng project origin from the loopback API of that copy and blocks every other origin, and the runner resolves the Enteng host to loopback, so nothing reaches a hosted project. Ids carry the suffix _ENTENG.
findings.R3_03_REMINDERS: Owner D16-1: the Reminder menu showed sample rows and was hidden in Enteng. It now reads and writes through the reminder facade (settings.reminder.view / settings.reminder.manage) that calls the accepted Native own-user reminder functions: create, edit, done, reopen, cancel, each changing exactly the reminder row, its audit row and the Native idempotency row; a resend with the same request answers the same and changes nothing; stale version, another user's reminder, a missing key and a role the Native actor rule refuses leave everything unchanged; due dates in WIB, filters and paging, a window over 200 said in words. Native, race, real Auth HTTP, browser desktop and phone (and on the Enteng build), oracles from Native rows.
findings.R3_03_ERP_SETTINGS: Owner D16-1: Pengaturan ERP showed sample settings and was hidden in Enteng. It now reads public.erp_cp7_get_erp_settings_v1 (read only: the 13 accessory and laundry policies with status, version, history and the official cutover date) and saves through the same Native writers the Aksesori and Laundry pages use (SET_POLICY); only the owner may change a policy (Native rule), ADMIN and the auditor read, values and reasons hidden from roles without the admin right. Cases: facade equals both Native tables, a save changes only that policy (+1 version, one event with the request id), same request once, stale version refused, two tabs one winner, non-owner refused by Native, refused without the view key, read-only and private; real Auth HTTP; browser desktop and phone as OWNER and AUDITOR_VIEW_ONLY (and on the Enteng build).
findings.R3_03_AUDIT_TRAIL: Owner D16-1: the Audit Trail menu (admin-audit) reads erp.audit_logs through the read facade erp_cp7_get_audit_trail_v1 (settings.audit.view; CSV of the shown rows only with settings.audit.export): closed query, newest first, a fixed as_of cutoff and keyset paging so writes after page 1 never move, repeat or hide a row; old/new data only in the detail of one row, withheld above 512 KB. Oracles read erp.audit_logs and erp.app_users directly.
findings.R3_03_CUSTOMER_HISTORY: Owner D16-1: the Riwayat Pelanggan menu (sales-history) reads through the read facade erp_cp7_get_customer_history_v1 (sales.history.view; amounts only with finance.ar.view, CSV only with sales.history.export): customer list and per-customer timeline of invoices, payments, returns and cancellations (WIB), one snapshot per answer; invoice figures defined as the receivables reader; a cancelled document without its audit row is refused in words. Oracles sum the Native sales tables directly.
findings.R3_03_WAREHOUSE_SUMMARY: Owner D16-1 (not an audit finding): Ringkasan Gudang showed sample figures and was hidden in Enteng. It now reads public.erp_cp7_get_warehouse_summary_v1: per location and kind the rows of Bahan & Roll without accessories, Aksesori and Ringkasan Barang Jadi with their own tables, filters and rounding, each section only with its screen key, values only with finance.hpp.view, and an attention list of Native facts behind the key of the screen that shows each (fabric below minimum needs master.fabric.view as well, which can be granted to Gudang in Pengguna & Hak Akses). One STABLE statement, one snapshot per answer. Cases: receipt and cutting equal raw rows and the three detail reads; values only with finance.hpp.view; sections per role key; refusals without warehouse.dashboard.view; attention equals Native tables after Native drafts; read-only and private; transfers committed during reads never give a half-applied answer; real Auth OWNER, GUDANG, a role without the key; browser desktop and phone as OWNER and GUDANG, on the test build and the Enteng build.
findings.R3_05_QC_AND_ACCESSORY_NOTE_BROWSER: Fable FABLE-016 remainder: QC & Final SKU and Nota Ambil Aksesori had no browser case on the connected screens. Three browser cases now drive them on real Auth and PostgREST (and again on the Enteng build): QC desktop and phone, where a role with production.final_sku.view but not .post sees the queue read-only and its own forced write is refused 403 with no effect, OWNER posts 10 GOOD and the Native rows show exactly one posted inspection, one lot, one +10 QC_GOOD movement, no BS case, balanced journals, and a resent request (dropped answer on desktop, direct on phone) gives the same answer with no second effect; and the accessory note deducted from payroll on desktop: a cancelled note is not deducted, the posted one is deducted exactly once, the note cannot be cancelled while the payroll is active, and paying from a bank funded with exactly the net leaves bank, receivable and payable at zero. Oracles read Native tables only.
findings.R3_03_SCREEN_CHAINS: Fable oracle 3 for owner D16-1: the business chains run on the screens alone, on real Auth and PostgREST (and again on the Enteng build), with every amount checked against Native rows: (a) sewing on WIP & Sewing -> Nota on Susun Nota FG -> count, approve and pay on Payroll & Kasbon -> Kas & Bank day totals -> Laporan cash and WIP -> close through the chain day on the Tutup Buku tab with 0 blockers, then reopen; seeded ADMIN sees the approved payroll without a pay button or the Tutup Buku tab; (b) on a phone, FG -> invoice -> full customer payment into a bank -> receipt on Kas & Bank -> Piutang Pelanggan Lunas, remaining Rp0; (c) the D14-2 (pay before accrual), D14-3/D15-1 (bank short by economic or by book date) and D15-5 (before the official cutover, on Jurnal & Transaksi Lain) guards refuse with their exact sentence and no Native change, and the lawful payment then goes through.
findings.R3_04_HPP_POOL: Sol KNOWN-R2-POOL-UI (S1), Astra ASTRA-C17-07 remainder (S2; S1 used): the Native pool writers had no screen or CP7 facade while the payroll guard told the user to cancel the pool first. 'Pool HPP absensi' on HPP & Rekalkulasi: Native preview or its refusal without figures, draft, activate, cancel (DRAFT -> VOIDED, ACTIVE -> CANCELLED with reversal), replacement pool (correction_of_pool_id) only through erp.create/activate/cancel_attendance_hpp_pool_v1; review token, reason, one answer per (actor, request) in an insert-only table, Owner/Admin with finance.hpp.view (+ finance.hpp.manage to write) checked before and after the locks, a period ending on or before closed_through refused for every action. Cases: preview READY = oracle figures and BLOCKED without figures, lifecycle = Native rows/journals/view/validator, draft void without journal, cancel -> source correction (Mandor C policy) -> replacement 1000/20 = 500 + 500, closed books refused atomically, right removed between read and save, same UUID once, changed review token, KEUANGAN/PRODUKSI_QC refused, private/immutable facade; two tabs activate and create, same UUID in two sessions; real Auth HTTP; browser desktop and phone (and on the Enteng build) with the source correction on Master Data -> Mandor and KEUANGAN seeing no pool section. findings.R4_01_PUBLIC_ROUTES: Astra ASTRA-R3-01 (r3 report, S1): the CP4 public wrappers erp_create/activate_attendance_hpp_pool_v1, still executable by the browser role, created and activated a pool in a closed period and after finance.hpp.manage was revoked, through real Auth and the Data API, while the CP7 facade refused both. Owner D14-9 lets the direct-erp revoke wait for CP7C only while those paths are unreachable from the internet. Family: of the 69 public non-CP7 routes the browser role may execute, 40 are called by the app (kept), 4 are the personal reminder routes two CP7 layers call (kept), and 25 are not called by the app; those 25 (cp7_public_routes_bundle.py) get one first statement that refuses a Data API session (session_user authenticator) with 42501 CP7_PUBLIC_ROUTE_CLOSED and the route name; definitions are captured and restored like every F03 predecessor delta, no grant changes, a database session is unchanged (the revoke batch stays CP7C, FABLE-012). verify() fails on any public route a browser role (authenticated or anon) may execute that is not reviewed. Cases: Astra's ASTRA_R3_POOL_PUBLIC_CLOSED_PERIOD and ASTRA_R3_POOL_PUBLIC_REVOKED_MANAGE as written (COUNTEREXAMPLE while the old route writes); all 25 refused through real Auth with their own name, nothing written, the app's routes still answer; the same pool calls as a database session reach the Native writer while a Data API session is refused (plpgsql and sql bodies); the app (src/) names exactly the 40 kept routes and none of the closed ones; a new public route, an anon-only route and a closed route recreated without its refusal each fail the review.
findings.R4_02_REOPEN_POSITIVE_INVERSE: Astra ASTRA-R2-01 remainder (r3 report, S1): a finished PO stayed blocked (FG_USED 2) after a +2 finished-goods adjustment and its own REVERSE, because reopen_po_snapshot counted every negative movement as a use minus its own reversals, so the -2 inverse of an inflow was a 'use'. The pairing now holds in both directions: a negative movement that is the reversal of a positive movement only takes back that inflow and is not counted; an unrelated inflow still never offsets an active use. Cases: Astra's ASTRA_R3_REOPEN_POSITIVE_ADJUSTMENT_INVERSE as written (COUNTEREXAMPLE while refused), an active sales draft after a reversed +2 still blocks with qty 2 (stock 10->12->10->8->10), reopen after +2/-2 then finish again gives the same stock, HPP and WIP balance, two tabs reopen once.
findings.R4_03_AUDIT_LATE_COMMIT: Astra ASTRA-R3-02 (r3 report, S2): the Audit Trail listing fixed its cutoff as the highest visible log id, but a sequence id is not a commit order: a lower id held open while a higher id committed (231 held, 232 committed) entered the cutoff after the first page, behind the cursor, and was never visited while snapshot.newer stayed false. Every listing now carries the mark of its rows inside the cutoff (count-sum of the matching ids, snapshot.listed, taken by the first page; the keyset cursor is '<id>:<mark>' and the request may send listed); a later page whose mark differs answers snapshot.changed=true and newer=true, and the screen stops paging and asks for Muat ulang. A mark without a cutoff, a cursor mark different from the one sent and a malformed cursor are refused (CP7_AUDIT_QUERY). Cases: Astra's ASTRA_R3_AUDIT_LOWER_ID_LATE_COMMIT schedule as written (COUNTEREXAMPLE while the late row is skipped silently), ordinary commit order keeps the mark and walks every row once, a late row outside the filter leaves the listing unchanged, the next listing shows all nine once, the refusals; DOM test of the stop-and-reload; the r3 browser case checks the new cursor.
findings.R4_04_TEXT_READABLE: Astra ASTRA-R3-03 (r3 report, S2): on the connected WIP & Sewing page the KPI figures, PO names and cut/sew facts were nearly white on white cards: the cards set background #fff and their text inherited the app's dark-theme foreground #f4f6fb. The light cards now set their own dark foreground (.cwip-kpis article, .cwip-workspace). The same family was found by a readability census on the demo build (Master Data > Pola: workspace and editor) and fixed the same way. Guard: every visible text is measured against the colour it is painted on (WCAG relative luminance; a gradient counts as each stop, the worst taken); below 2:1 is refused on every menu, desktop and phone, in CP17 browser cases on the connected build with real rows (and the Enteng build), and in the UI phone width census of the demo build; the WIP figures Astra named must reach 4.5:1.
findings.R4_05_INTERNAL_GUARD_ONE_PROBE: Owner D17-1 (Sol KNOWN-P19-DIRECT-LATENCY: 'Ambil analisis ERP terbaru' with financial figures 7.4-8 s at 100 targets, stopped by the 8 s limit at 300). Function counters of one direct capture (CI run 39157467151): the protected owner report calls erp.require_internal() about 32,000 times per capture (erp.account_id per checked row), and the CP7 stack had grown the guard to one query per private command context table (ten): 3.9 s of the capture's 6.3 s. The guard now answers the case without a context row of this backend and transaction first: a transaction without a transaction id has written none, otherwise one probe of the same ten tables with the same identity filters; then only the unchanged final role test decides. With any row present the unchanged dispatch runs, every check and fine refusal in place. Install: last delta of the F03 stack after a hash check of the guard body in place (cp7_internal_guard_bundle.py); uninstall restores the Native guard through the replayed originals. Guard: verify() proves the dispatch holds only admitting context branches (one CASE each, identity filters first) and that the probe reads exactly their tables; Native cases call the installed guard and the same guard without its probe side by side for eight callers (owner, unknown user, service role, a sales context row of this transaction and its fine refusal CP7_SALES_ACCESS_DENIED, a procurement row without the right, rows of another backend or transaction) and require equal answers, and a guard with a context branch the probe does not read, another statement in the dispatch or no probe fails the review. Writer-local PG16 (throwaway, stub tables): 27 callers equal; 89-103 us per call before, 29 us without a transaction id and 45 us with one after.
findings.R5_01_PAYROLL_CHECK_KNOWS_FG_REPAIR: Sol SOL-R4-001 (S1, r4 report audit/sol_cp17_r4): a valid FG_REPAIR Nota (two AX repair wages of 2 and 1 pcs at 2,000, saved and posted through erp_cp7_save_nota_v1, 6,000) raised two CRITICAL payroll_work_wrong_contractor, because erp.run_v263a_payroll_integrity_checks() resolved a Nota line's contractor only through PRODUCTION (work completion event) and REWORK (rework order); AX taught the eligible-lines view, the source CHECK, the validator and the merge the FG_REPAIR source but not this checker. Forward delta on that one Native function (cp7_payroll_checks_bundle.py, anchor checked, captured and restored through the replayed originals): an FG_REPAIR line resolves through its repair wage, like the validator; a line whose wage is missing or belongs to another contractor still counts. Cases: Sol's case as written (CP17_R5_01_VALID_FG_REPAIR_NOTA_ZERO_ALARM_SOL: same fixture, same resolved rows, detector delta must be none, COUNTEREXAMPLE while the false alarm is there; the checker as it was before R5-01 runs beside the installed one on the same books and must count the two lines), and a control (CP17_R5_01_PAYROLL_CHECK_STILL_FINDS_WRONG_OR_MISSING_REPAIR: a wage moved to another contractor and a missing wage each count once; the immutable-wage guard is off only inside a rolled-back savepoint, labelled DETECTOR_CONTROL).
findings.R5_02_REPORT_READERS_ACCOUNT_LOOKUP_ONCE: Owner D17-2 (KNOWN-P19-DIRECT-LATENCY: direct analysis with financial figures 4.25-5.92 s at 100 targets in the r4 retests). Function counters of one direct capture with figures at 100 targets (r4 qualification run 39173212515): 4.56 s server, erp.account_id(text) 30,974 calls, 2.48 s with its guard, because eleven STABLE report and check readers (run_v268, run_v267, the HPP books, the owner report, the opening and pocket checks) write erp.account_id('<KEY>') inline in per-row filters. In those readers every literal call becomes (select erp.account_id('<KEY>')), an uncorrelated init plan evaluated once per query (cp7_report_accounts_bundle.py; install checks the literal call count of each reader and that every key is a core mapping, which the Native guard keeps from being deleted or renamed; captured and restored through the replayed originals). Writer-local PG16: 66,008 calls -> 12, same rows. Cases: CP17_R5_02_REPORT_READERS_SAME_ANSWER (each installed reader and the same reader without the change side by side on the CP17 books, every product, PO, pocket period, opening settlement, sale journal/PO pair and three report windows: same rows or same refusal; the CP17 books hold no opening credit, pocket period or sale journal, so the first run at 3b9817ae compared three readers on no input: the case now builds, inside its rolled-back savepoint and through the BB/BE probe paths, an opening import with three allowances and a customer credit applied, a production import with its historical pocket period posted, and a sale of an opening finished good with its return, and every reader must answer at least one input without a refusal, those three with a value) and CP17_R5_02_REPORT_READERS_REVIEWED (a reader with one more call, an unlisted key or already wrapped text is refused; the install refuses a changed reader; a core mapping cannot be deleted).
